newsitem.title: UK: Oil bounces back in late European refinery buying.
newsitem.headline: Oil bounces back in late European refinery buying.

text.p: World oil prices bounced back on Tuesday, despite warmer than expected weather in the key United States markets, underlining how vulnerable oil markets have been this year to the merest whiff of a supply shortfall.
London February futures for bellwether North Sea Brent blend rose 20 cents to finish a truncated Christmas eve session at $23.39 a barrel.
Dealers said a seasonal chill in European markets had sent buyers scurrying for cover just in case demand soared again after the holiday season.
"On the face of it there's plenty of supply around but no-one's taking any risks," said a futures broker.
Spot European physical crude markets have seen brisk business in the normally quiet pre-Christmas period with some 20 million barrels of North Sea crude trading in two days.
Dealers said the failure of oil prices to show any significant declines despite the long-awaited return of Iraqi exports had probably pushed refiners into making some last-minute purchases.
"Some refiners have been waiting until the last minute in the hope that Iraqi crude would move prices their way but it just hasn't happened."
Prices all year have been supported by a worldwide trend toward just-in-time inventory management which has often left oil stocks looking perilously thin.
Iraq has loaded four tankers of crude in the 10 days since exports resumed under the United Nations' oil-for-food exchange.
The United Nations has approved 18 contracts for about 500,000 barrels a day of crude exports, enough at current prices for the $2 billion worth of sales Iraq is allowed over a six month period.
